scope: Validate the PROC-301 process documentation (PROCESS.md + heir.yaml) against the current Unified Template (6th locked constant at law/UNIFIED_TEMPLATE.md) and the Grid Reader Pattern (law/doctrine/GRID_READER_PATTERN.md). Identify structural gaps, section misalignment, missing sections, and non-conformance. The Unified Template defines 14 sections in 3 clusters (Identity/Contract/Governance mapped to Thing/Flow/Change). The Grid Reader Pattern defines PROC-301's role as an Updater in the People sub-hub — requirements for baseline timestamps, change detection timestamps, and grid-as-view compliance apply.

intent: Validate PROC-301 documentation against Unified Template (the 6th locked constant) and Grid Reader Pattern requirements. Operator specified 'v6.0.0' — the Unified Template file itself does not carry a version number; the subject currently declares Template Version 4.0.0. The file at law/UNIFIED_TEMPLATE.md IS the standard regardless of version label. Grid Reader Pattern is DRAFT status but defines the Updater role that PROC-301 fills in the outreach domain.

acceptance_criteria: PROCESS.md sections match Unified Template 14-section / 3-cluster structure
All 10 invariant-set layers from US handoff have corresponding sections with correct schemas
HEIR in heir.yaml has all 8 required fields per law/heir_schema.yaml
DMJ section (Section 6) present with Define/Map/Join tables
Grid Reader Updater requirements met: baseline timestamps documented, change detection approach specified, grid-as-view compliance (writes to sub-hub tables, grid reads)
All comparators (C_1 through C_7) traceable to invariant set layers
ORBT gate rules complete with all 4 transitions

structural_gaps_detected.detail: Unified Template Section 6 (DMJ — Define, Map, Join) is absent from the subject. The subject embeds Key Builder concepts in the IMO Middle steps but does not have the explicit three-table DMJ structure (Define table L19, Map table L20, Join table L21) required by the template and the US invariant set layer L10.

Subject uses 1-14 numbering with non-standard names (WHY THIS EXISTS vs PURPOSE, WHAT IT GRABS OFF THE WALL vs RESOURCES, OSAM vs DATA SCHEMA, SMOKE TEST vs VERIFICATION). Unified Template uses different section numbers and names.
Unified Template groups sections into 3 clusters: IDENTITY (Thing), CONTRACT (Flow), GOVERNANCE (Change). Subject has no cluster headers — sections are flat-listed.

heir.yaml has 7 fields but is missing 4 of the 8 required fields (imo_topology, services, secrets_provider, acceptance_criteria) and contains 4 non-standard fields (heir_ref, sub_hub, component, created_at).
Unified Template Section 3 (RESOURCES) includes Dependencies + Downstream Consumers + Tools + Secrets as one section. Subject splits Dependencies into its own Section 8.

structural_gaps_detected.gap: Grid Reader timestamp fields not documented
structural_gaps_detected.detail: Grid Reader Pattern requires two timestamps per field (last_checked, last_changed) for Updater processes. Subject's OSAM section does not document these timestamp fields in the WRITE table. The writes mention person_found_at and linkedin_found_at but not the Grid Reader canonical timestamp pair.
Unified Template Data Schema section requires a Join Chain (tree notation from spine ID). Subject has READ/WRITE/Forbidden Paths but no Join Chain subsection.

strengths_detected: IMO Declaration is thorough: two-question intake answered, 7-step Middle table with all 5 columns, Circle section present
Comparators well-defined: 7 comparators with C_i notation, tolerances k_i, primitives assigned, decision function P_301(x;θ) stated
Constants & Variables section follows Bedrock §2 with mathematical definitions
ORBT gate rules present with all 4 transitions
Sigma tracking table present (awaiting data from runs)
Execution trace schema referenced (14 fields, append-only)
Session log with 6 entries documenting build history
Stop conditions include Strike 3 → AD escalation
